skill.name: video-sync
skill.description: Combines source video with shot-analysis data to produce a synchronized review video with readable shot details.
skill.summary: Create an annotated video where the footage and synchronized shot information stay visible together.
skill.author: eternityspring

security_audit.summary: All 175 static patterns were reviewed against the implementation and judged false positives from expected local media processing, documentation examples, test fixtures, or escaped rendering logic. No prompt injection, unauthorized data access, command injection, or malicious exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Command execution remains security-sensitive even though the current calls use fixed binaries and argument arrays.
remediation.suggestion: Keep using execFileSync without a shell, validate all user-supplied paths, and reject unexpected executable overrides.

remediation.issue: The panel renderer uses innerHTML for generated rows and labels.
remediation.suggestion: Retain the existing escaping helper, keep color values sourced from fixed dictionaries, and preserve the XSS regression tests.

remediation.issue: Media and frame paths can refer to local files selected by the operator.
remediation.suggestion: For automated multi-user deployments, restrict inputs and outputs to an approved workspace before invoking ffprobe, Chrome, or ffmpeg.

不用碰脚本、不用重新想截图逻辑。样式约定见 `{baseDir}/references/panel-style.md`。
对不上通常是 shots.json 和原片不是同一条,或者 `--video` 指错了。

content.value_statement: Shot notes are difficult to compare with footage when they live in separate files. This skill combines both into a synchronized video with an animated shot panel.
actual_capabilities: Reads shots.json data and matches shot details to the source video.
Builds landscape layouts with video above the information panel.
Builds portrait layouts with video beside the information panel.
Keeps shot rows synchronized with cut points during playback.
Uses ffmpeg and a headless browser without npm dependencies.
Preserves the source audio track when one is present.
limitations: Requires Node.js, ffmpeg, ffprobe, and Chrome or a compatible browser.
Expects shots.json to match the source video duration and content.
Does not perform shot detection, editing, transitions, music, or subtitles.
Large shot lists may require a larger panel or segmented review.

use_cases.title: Review Shot Coverage
use_cases.description: Create a synchronized reference video for checking shot composition, timing, camera movement, and visual continuity.

use_cases.title: Present Storyboard Findings
use_cases.description: Share footage with shot notes attached to the exact moments discussed during production reviews.

use_cases.title: Audit Video Analysis
use_cases.description: Turn structured shot-analysis data into a readable deliverable for research, teaching, or archive work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Sync Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use video-sync to combine the source video with its matching shots.json file and export an annotated review video.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow with default layout settings

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Layout Language
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the synchronized video in English, use the provided frames directory for thumbnails, and report the output path and dimensions.

prompt_templates.title: Tune the Review Panel
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the video layout, increase the panel ratio for readability, render the panels, and compose the final video with the chosen settings.

prompt_templates.title: Validate the Final Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Export the synchronized video, inspect representative frames at early, middle, and late timestamps, and summarize any shot or highlight mismatches.

output_examples.input: A source video, matching shots.json file, and optional frames directory.
output_examples.output: An annotated MP4 with the footage and synchronized shot information displayed together.

output_examples.input: A portrait video with English labels and a requested wider information panel.
output: A final video path with dimensions and duration.

output_examples.input: A completed export that needs a visual quality check.
output_examples.output: A concise validation report covering timing alignment, active-row highlighting, layout, and missing thumbnails.

best_practices: Confirm that shots.json and the source video describe the same recording before rendering.
Run the planning step first and adjust panel size when shot descriptions are difficult to read.
Inspect representative frames after export to verify shot alignment and active-row highlighting.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to detect shots or create a shots.json file.
Do not assume a successful render proves that shot data matches the footage.
Do not use tiny panel settings when the review depends on long descriptions or dense metadata.

faq.question: What input does the skill require?
faq.answer: It requires a source video and a matching shots.json file. A frames directory is optional.

faq.question: Which video orientations are supported?
faq.answer: Landscape and square videos place the panel below the footage. Portrait videos place it beside the footage.

faq.question: Does it preserve audio?
faq.answer: Yes. The original audio track is copied into the composed video when the source contains audio.

faq.question: Does it detect shots?
faq.answer: No. It consumes shot analysis produced by another workflow, such as video-shots.

faq.question: Can the panel design be changed?
faq.answer: Yes. Edit scripts/panel.css and render the panels again to apply layout and styling changes.

faq.question: What should I check before sharing the result?
faq.answer: Check the output dimensions, duration, shot alignment, active-row movement, and any missing thumbnails.
